artifacts.summary: Implementation summary: subdivide_chunk() early-return removal, section07 re-chunk (1 -> 94 chunks), stale DB row handling, and full no-regression verification.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed literature-chunk.sh's subdivide_chunk() oversized-atomic-block branch to fall through to size-based subdivision instead of returning unsplit; re-chunked baier_katoen_2008 section07 from 1 giant 46,176-token chunk to 94 correctly-sized chunks matching siblings, with no regression to the other 11 sections or 93 other covered directories.

memory_candidates.content: In literature-chunk.sh, subdivide_chunk() classifies a chunk as 'atomic' if its first line or title matches an atomic-block regex (e.g. theorem/definition headers). If an oversized atomic-classified chunk is meant to still be split, do not return early after the warning print -- let control fall through to the paragraph/sentence subdivision path. A PDF-page-split artifact (e.g. a stray 'Theorem N.NN.' line at the very start of a whole-section chunk) can cause otherwise-normal sections to be misclassified as atomic and skip subdivision entirely.

literature-build-index.sh --global is a full from-scratch rebuild: it writes a fresh .literature.db.tmp from every on-disk chunks.json manifest and atomically renames it over the live DB. It does NOT perform an incremental INSERT-OR-REPLACE against the existing DB's prior contents. Any manual DELETE against the live DB immediately before running --global is superseded by the rebuild and has no lasting effect -- to remove a stale row, the correct source of truth to edit is the manifest (chunks.json) on disk, not the DB directly.

literature-chunk.sh's chunk_id is NOT a full-content hash; it is deterministic on doc_id/section_path/title (or similar structural fields), so two chunks with different content but the same section_path/title (e.g. the same opening line) can regenerate the identical chunk_id. When verifying that a 'stale' chunk row has been replaced, check the row's content/token_count rather than asserting the chunk_id itself is absent.
